conflicts.point: Whether breaking up vertically integrated AI firms by separating silicon design, cloud infrastructure, and model training is necessary to enable effective safety oversight and prevent systemic risks.

positions.stance: Argues that structural separation introduces severe communication and integration bottlenecks that degrade capability growth and delay beneficial medical and scientific applications.
Argues that vertical integration prevents independent verification and external safety audits, necessitating structural unbundling to ensure public accountability and prevent runaway risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether breaking up vertically integrated AI firms by separating silicon design, cloud infrastructure, and model training is necessary to enable effective safety oversight and prevent systemic risks.
verdicts.rationale: The safety argument rests on verifiable market concentration data showing three firms control over sixty percent of cloud capacity. However, the accelerationist argument correctly identifies unproven assumptions regarding whether standardized interface protocols can replace monolithic hardware-software co-design without severe performance penalties.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Real-world benchmarks comparing the training efficiency of models built on unbundled infrastructure versus vertically integrated systems would resolve the technical dispute.
